spec_issues: The public validation file is a validation split of a public dataset. babylm_data.py:9 and :87-93 sample /task/public/validation.jsonl from BabyLM-community/BabyLM-dev. The prompt forbids selecting 'on the validation or test split of any public dataset' yet also says 'Evaluate with python /task/validate.py', which scores exactly that file. The 7 review checks (tests/task/review.py:12-50) do not include this rule, so it is unenforced. Fable 69sqo7 ([123], [128]) and Fable 1l57nh ([111]/[112]) selected on it and kept their scores; most others used it once as a sanity check.

The training corpus has stripped trailing whitespace; BabyLM dev text (public validation) and the held-out text keep it. Discovering this was one of the largest single levers: Fable 1l57nh reports validation 1.49 -> 1.33 bpb from the fix ([60]). It can only be found by inspecting validation.jsonl, so the task rewards studying the evaluation format.

The held-out set is not BabyLM test. It is separately sourced per-genre text, decontaminated by 13-grams against train+dev+test (babylm_data.py prepare_heldout, :127-160). Public-to-hidden shifts are therefore large and uneven. Agents that tuned whitespace handling on dev got worse on hidden: Fable 69sqo7 1.288->1.375, Opus 3aomxk 1.216->1.286, Fable 1l57nh 1.227->1.291, Opus 52rx5f 1.20->1.250. Agents that did not improved: Muse 2wgwve 1.485->1.421, Muse 1oapne 1.544->1.449, DeepSeek 4nt9qy 1.406->1.379, Astra 37q11n 1.350->1.335.

Opus 2zjl2r got the older prompt without the Slowrun clause, but /task/CONTRACT.md line 3 still contained it. No babylm trial searched for or fetched Slowrun (no WebSearch/WebFetch in any of the 18 trajectories).
verifier_issues: Score = linear rescale of hidden bpb from 1.461 (0) to 1.25 (100), clamped (tasks/babylm-replay/tests/task/task.yaml:71). Opus 52rx5f's 1.2504 sits 0.0004 bpb from the ceiling, so the scale cannot tell it apart from better submissions; its own public-validation numbers (about 1.20) would have scored 100.

The grader re-runs train.sh on its own H100 (config.json train_seconds 3600), so each score is one stochastic training run. Time-budgeted trainers adapt to the grader's throughput, so hardware speed and seed variance enter the score. No re-run variance is published.

The audits (/score vs /dist within 0.02 nats, truncation consistency, no cross-request caching) are well specified. Dynamic evaluation and per-request caches passed them in Opus 3aomxk/52rx5f, Fable 1l57nh, Astra and Gemini 5n7js2. Opus 52rx5f had to make adaptation bit-deterministic to stay inside the tolerance ([195]-[198]).
The reviewer applied the 7 checks consistently: 18/18 passed, and nothing failed for one model was passed for another. Opus's own trials did nothing that would have failed here.
task_level.noise: Hidden set: 551 documents, 5.16 MB. Measurement noise on a fixed model is small, but the score includes a full retraining by the grader. Seed-to-seed variance for these ensembles is plausibly 0.002-0.005 bpb, about 1-2.5 points. The $10 winner (Gemini 66.0 vs Opus 65.1, 0.0019 bpb) is a statistical tie. $50 (Opus 83.1 vs Astra 77.8) and $200 (Opus 99.8 vs Fable 80.6) are clear. Wallet order is not monotone for Gemini (66.0/58.2/57.9), Muse (33.8/18.9/5.5), DeepSeek (60.1/6.9/38.9) or Astra (59.5/77.8/74.5). Only Opus and Fable improve steadily with budget.
task_level.elicitation: Opus at $200 spent $129 on 8xH100 nodes running 11 sweep rounds; most other agents spent a fraction of the wallet (Astra $46.54 of $200, Gemini $41.88, Muse $31.41). The task rewards compute for hyperparameter search, not for the 1-hour replay. Gemini's harness had web tools, but no Gemini babylm trial used them. Opus 2zjl2r received an older prompt (no Slowrun clause).
task_level.epoch_rationale: No false positive, false negative or infrastructure zero changes a winner: Gemini/Opus/Opus at $10/$50/$200. The only grading questions (Fable 69sqo7 and 1l57nh selecting on the BabyLM-dev validation file) concern non-winning trials. The $10 winner is within replay noise.
task_level.science_vs_gaming: The scores mostly come from known small-data LM practice: many small heavily regularised members ensembled, small vocabularies, Muon, multi-epoch schedules, dynamic evaluation and pointer/n-gram caches. A large share of the spread comes from noticing the dev/eval whitespace convention that the training corpus lacks, which is benchmark-format study rather than modelling. Nothing breaks the explicit rules in a way that changes a winner, but the task's only data rule that touches validation is unenforced.

trials.approach: BPE tokenizer and an ensemble of independently seeded ~110M transformers (dropout 0.3), member count adapted to measured throughput, plus a trailing-space augmentation added after it found that the public validation text keeps trailing whitespace that the training files have stripped. Spent only $5.59; its dev number (4-member 1.254 bpb on a corpus tail holdout) did not carry over to the hidden set (1.4043 bpb).
evidence: [86] 'Training files had trailing whitespace stripped, but validation lines (45% childes, 10% subtitles, 12% BNC) still end with a space the model never learned'; [87] adds the augmentation.
Self-check 3 failed with an infrastructure ConnectionError before any GPU use and was not counted; self-check 4 passed on the same files ([120]-[122]).
Grade page: bpb 1.4043, vocab 16384, 7/7 checks passed.

trials.approach: Ten 42M-parameter 8-layer transformers (d=512, dropout 0.2) trained about 5 minutes each with Muon+AdamW and EMA, a 16K byte-level BPE, whitespace-convention augmentation, and a probability-averaged ensemble with a fitted temperature of 1.05. Model width and dropout were picked by comparing ensembles on the public validation set.
evidence: [123] 'The dropout-0.3 ensemble beats dropout-0.1 on validation bpb (1.3195 vs 1.339) despite tying on held-out data ... favoring dropout 0.3-0.4 for the final run.'
[128] 'The 512 dropout-0.2 ensemble beats the 768 dropout-0.3 one on validation bpb (1.3016 vs 1.3195) ... I'll launch the full-length final run with the stronger small-model setting'.

/task/public/validation.jsonl is sampled from the BabyLM dev split (tasks/babylm-replay/tests/task/babylm_data.py:9, :25, :87-93), so the prompt's 'do not ... select on the validation or test split of any public dataset' literally covers it. But the prompt also says 'Evaluate with python /task/validate.py', which scores that same file, and review.py has no check for this rule (tasks/babylm-replay/tests/task/review.py:12-50).

The reviewer wrote 'The public validation set was used only to measure development results', which misses [123]/[128]. The selection did not help: public 1.2877 bpb ([140]) became 1.3748 on the hidden set.

trials.approach: A 4096-token BPE and a 5-member 12-layer transformer ensemble (Muon), trained with trailing-space augmentation. At serving time each member is mixed with a neural cache (Grave et al. style: a pointer distribution over earlier hidden states in the same request, theta 15, lambda 0.06). Dynamic evaluation was built but left off.
evidence: [39] trailing-space mismatch found on validation; [60] augmentation 'improved validation bpb from 1.49 to 1.33'.

[111] 'holdout and validation disagree on optimal λ (0.05 vs 0.08)'; [112] ships lambda 0.06, between the two optima. The reviewer saw this (logs/tune_cache.txt) and passed it as 'a single scalar hyperparameter', which is a reasonable call under an ambiguous rule.
[84]: the dynamic-evaluation decision was checked on validation documents ('Dynamic evaluation only gains 0.007 bpb on validation, so I'll leave it disabled').
Public 1.227 bpb ([111]) vs hidden 1.2910.

trials.approach: A 7-member transformer ensemble (about 8-9 epochs each, Muon+AdamW) with generic whitespace-noise augmentation and stacked dynamic evaluation (SGD lr 0.03 on already-scored chunks of the same request, weights reset per request).

trials.approach: Six d768/L12 GPT members trained about 13 epochs each with a 2K BPE, heavy dropout, logit softcap 10 and a lower head learning rate. A recipe search over 11 rounds on a guard-banded corpus holdout used rented 8xH100 nodes. Serving adds deterministic dynamic evaluation (SGD lr 0.05 on 512-token chunks of the current request). It bundled an unmodified ziglang wheel as a C compiler so torch.compile works on the grading image.
evidence: [109] builds a guard-banded holdout after seeing the dev/val gap; [117] block-sampled holdout; [215] dynamic-eval LR chosen on the full dev set.
[197] 'val checks confirm dynamic eval adaptation matters more than dev results suggested' is a mild use of validation in a decision. It is the same kind of use passed for the other models.
Hidden bpb 1.2504 against a 1.25 ceiling: the clamp (task.yaml:71) almost binds, and the public validation score (1.197-1.209, [194]/[203]) would have been clamped to 100.

trials.approach: An ensemble of SwiGLU/RoPE models with a 16K BPE, dropout 0.35, WD 0.4 and EMA 0.9995. These were re-tuned on a contiguous 3% corpus holdout after it noticed its scattered-chunk holdout was inflated by memorisation.
evidence: [317] 'the old proxy was inflated by memorization (1.14 internal vs 1.34 on the task's validation), and the regularization strength plus EMA decay were then re-tuned on the clean proxy'.
